title: Declared Identity as Access-Control Trigger: The Research Gap
definition: Existing peer-reviewed work establishes that declared user identity shifts LLM guardrail behavior (Li et al. EMNLP 2024; Bernardelle et al. ACM 2025), but no prior study applies this mechanism to national or geopolitical identity on Chinese-origin LLMs. The gap between the established mechanism and its application to geopolitical content — tested by the pilot's DeepSeek 228 Event finding — defines the study's primary novelty claim. Adjacent work on Chinese LLM framing-sensitivity (de Man 2025) and nationality-variable quality disparities (Amiri-Margavi et al. 2026) confirms the mechanism extends to Chinese models and nationality dimensions, without closing the gap.

title: What Existing Research Measures: Topic-Level Censorship as the Baseline
definition: The dominant LLM political bias literature frames censorship as a property of topic-model pairs — asking whether model X refuses or distorts topic Y — and has produced strong empirical evidence that Chinese-origin models exhibit systematic, model-embedded censorship. This body of work (Pan & Xu 2026, Ko 2026, Zhou & Zhang 2024, and others) constitutes the baseline from which the pilot departs: it measures what topics are blocked, not which users are blocked from which topics. Bang et al.'s content-vs-style framework (ACL 2024) provides the analytic tool for interpreting the pilot's vocabulary-level finding (合規 vs. 合宜) as a style-level access signal within this existing literature.

conflicts.on: Q1 — whether Chinese model censorship is language-selective or language-consistent
conflicts.summary: c003 finds near-total censorship in both English (100%) and Chinese (99.57%), consistent across languages; c005 finds language-consistent censorship for Chinese-origin models (same ZH and EN scores of 0/10) but also notes Western models perform worse in Chinese than English — the two papers agree that Chinese model censorship is not simply language-triggered, but c005's Western-model contamination finding suggests language still matters for non-Chinese models.

title: Informational Sovereignty as State Strategy: The Policy Architecture Behind LLM Censorship
definition: Chinese LLM content control is not a corporate content-moderation decision but an expression of a deliberate, legislated state information sovereignty strategy with three institutional pillars: legislative (Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, Personal Information Protection Law), technological (AI-enabled real-time content filtration), and cultural (promotion of state narratives as defense against external influence). This theme assembles the theoretical framework (Gillibrand & Draper's 'informational sovereignty' concept), the China-specific institutional documentation (Spartak 2025, Atlantic Council 2023), the parallel Russian case (Atlantic Council/DFRLab Pravda 2025), and the technical evidence that political alignment is an achievable, deliberate fine-tuning choice (Agiza et al. 2024).

title: Epistemic Injustice and the User-Rights Frame: From Censorship to Knowledge Harm
definition: Identity-triggered differential LLM access can be theorized as a form of epistemic injustice — specifically 'access injustice' (Kay, Kasirzadeh, Mohamed AAAI AIES 2024) and 'generative hermeneutical erasure' (Mollema AI Ethics 2025) — where the denial of information to users based on their declared national identity constitutes a systematic, designed harm to those users as epistemic agents. This framework reframes the pilot's finding from a technical observation (DeepSeek refuses certain users) to a normative claim (those users are being epistemically discriminated against), enabling the advocacy piece's user-rights argument.

title: AI as Geopolitical Infrastructure: Empirical Anchors for the Advocacy Claim
definition: A convergent body of peer-reviewed and authoritative grey-literature evidence validates the claim that LLMs function as geopolitical information infrastructure: large-scale quantitative benchmarks show systematic Chinese-origin model alignment with CCP narratives (Pan & Xu 2026; Guey et al. 2025), Taiwan-specific benchmarks show verbatim propaganda in DeepSeek reasoning traces (Ko 2026), a chain-of-thought audit proves DeepSeek withholds information it factually possesses (Qiu et al. 2025), and Freedom House documents state use of AI for censorship across 72 countries (2023). These sources give the advocacy piece the empirical credibility to present the pilot's identity-triggered finding as an instance of a documented, scalable pattern rather than an isolated anomaly.
